nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ni(OH)₂/CuₓO growth
nodes.procedure: Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (2 mmol), Cu(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (2 mmol) NH₄F (10 mmol) and urea (25 mmol) were dissolved in 40 mL water and stirred for 2 h. Then, the solution and as-prepared Cu(OH)₂ NWs@CF was moved into a Teflon-lined stainless autoclave, which held at 120°C for 6 h in an electric oven. The Ni(OH)₂/CuₓO was taken out after the reaction and washed with water and ethanol, then dried.

nodes.name: Gas-solid phosphating
nodes.procedure: Using the gas-solid phosphating method, Ni(OH)₂/CuₓO@CF was placed in downstream of the tube furnace, and 0.2 g of NaH₂PO₄ was placed in upstream of the heating device. Under a nitrogen gas atmosphere, the temperature was raised to 350°C and kept 1 h.

nodes.source_text: The OER activities of samples in each synthesis step were measured in 1 M KOH electrolyte with three-electrode system... The LSV curve with iR-compensated in Fig. 3a displays that Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF can yield 50 mA cm⁻² and 100 mA cm⁻² at the overpotential of 330 mV (η₅₀) and 400 mV (η₁₀₀) respectively... The derived Tafel slope of Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF is 72 mVdec⁻¹... The calculated C_dl of Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF is up to 22.8 mFcm⁻²... The chronoamperometric measurement was performed at a constant potential of 1.7 vs RHE without iR-compensated. During 28-hour OER operation, the current density is relatively stable.

The HER activity of as-prepared catalysts was further tested in 1 M KOH electrolyte. The LSV curves in Fig. 3g exhibits that the Cu₃P/Ni₂P@CF possesses a dramatic HER activity, and it only demands an overpotential of 88.1 mV to attain 10 mAcm⁻²... A small Tafel slope of about 94 mVdec⁻¹ was obtained... To examine the HER stability of Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF, a constant potential of -1.1 vs RHE without iR-compensated was adopted. Almost no attenuation of current density was observed during the uninterrupted 24-hour operation.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting (EOWS) performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: In view of the superb OER and HER activities of Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF, two-electrode electrolytic cell for EOWS in 1 M KOH was constructed... The Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF || Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF can reach 10 mAcm⁻² at a cell voltage of only 1.56 V... The long-term stability of Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF||Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF was verified by current density retention of 97.3% after a 68 h stability test (see Fig. 4c)... 6.9 mL H₂ and 3.45 mL O₂ were produced at constant current of 50 mA cm⁻² after 20 min for Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF||Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF electrolytic cell, which leads to the Faraday efficiency for both HER and OER close to 100%.

nodes.description: Nyquist plots for OER charge transfer resistance
nodes.source_text: Nyquist plots were conducted at overpotentials of 420 mV and 200 mV for OER and HER. ... Fig. 3e displays the Nyquist plots of the catalysts, in which the semicircle in the low-frequency scope represents the charge transfer resistance of the catalyst-electrolyte interface (R_ct). The result shows that the Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF possesses the smallest R_ct among all synthesized materials.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals hierarchical nanosheets with attenuated cylindrical structure after gas-solid phosphating for Cu₃P/Ni₂P@CF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: after the gas-solid phosphating, the hierarchical nanosheets almost maintain except with the attenuated of cylindrical structure for Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF sample (Fig. 1d, 1e and S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows hierarchical nanosheets morphology for Cu₃P/Ni₂P@CF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM and (f) HRTEM image of Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM displays heterogeneous interface with lattice fringes of 0.221 nm (111) plane of Ni₂P and 0.23 nm (202) plane of Cu₃P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM of Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF (Fig. 1f) displays that there exists self-evident heterogeneous interface including the distinct lattice fringes, in which the interplanar spacings are 0.221 nm and 0.23 nm , corresponding to the (111) plane for Ni₂P and (202) planes for Cu₃P , respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows uniform dispersion of Cu, Ni, P elements on the entire surface of Cu₃P/Ni₂P@CF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDX mapping of Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF manifests that the Cu, Ni, P elements are uniformly dispersed on the entire surface (Fig. 1g-1j).

As for Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF the diffraction peaks located at 36° 39° 41.6° 45.1° 46.2° 47.3° can be assigned to (112) (202) (211) (300) (113) (212) crystal planes of Cu₃P PDF#71-2261), while the characteristic peaks located at 40.8° 47.3° 54.2° 66.3° can be indexed to the a series of phases derived from Ni₂P (PDF#03-0953) (Fig. 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks at 853.3 eV (2p₃/₂) and 870.7 eV (2p₁/₂) for Niᵟ⁺ in Ni₂P, Cu 2p peaks at 932.3 eV and 952 eV for Cu-P in Cu₃P, P 2p peaks at 129.5 eV (reduced P) and 134 eV (oxidized P).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the high-resolution Ni 2p spectrum of Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF shows the deconvoluted peaks at 853.3 and 870.7 eV , which are ascribed to the Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ of Niᵟ⁺ in Ni₂P ... six peaks were observed for Cu 2p spectrum of Cu₃P/ Ni₂P@CF , corresponding to the Cu-P (932.3 eV, 952 eV for 2p₃/₂ and Cu₁/₂ in Cu₃P ... the XPS spectrum of P 2p in Cu₃P / Ni₂P@CF manifests two peaks at 129.5 eV and 134 eV .
